newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Amnesty launches year-long campaign on refugees.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty launches year-long campaign on refugees.

text.p: Amnesty International on Wednesday launched a year-long campaign to highlight the plight of the world's refugees.

"We want to remind the world that refugees are real people with real fears. People who have had to take the terrible decision to leave their homes, their communities and their countries because they fear for their lives," Amnesty Secretary General Pierre Sane said in a statement.
"They need protection and help, not indifference and rejection," he added.

Sane said at the launch of the campaign that Amnesty wanted to ensure that all asylum-seekers had a real chance to make their case through fair and impartial procedures and that no one would be sent back to a country where he or she ran the risk of suffering gross violations of human rights.

He said contrary to public perception 90 per cent of refugees live in the southern hemisphere, with African countries sheltering more than twice as many refugees as Europe, North America and Australia combined.
Yet countries everywhere were turning them away, sometimes forcibly as seen in Italy which had been expelling Albanians fleeing chaos in their own country, he added.

Sane said despite unabating human rights violations that force people into exile and the growing number of people needing international protection, governments were stepping up their efforts to keep them out.
"Governments may have a right to control their borders. But, having signed international conventions to protect refugees, they do not have the right to refuse access to asylum procedures," Sane said.
"Government policies are deliberately designed to deny safe havens to people faced with imprisonment, brutality and even murder if they are forcibly returned to their own countries," he added.
